title: Id allocation must be worktree-aware and ledger-backed under a common-dir lock (DEC-179 part 1)
description:
DEC-179 part (1), closing measurement (m1): allocation is refs-aware only, so two sessions on two worktrees of one repository that each create before committing both mint N+1, and the merge is an add/add conflict on the same .quest/tasks/

-.json path. Current code: nextTaskId and highestSequenceOnOtherRefs, plus nextDraftId, in src/cli/main.ts; nextPlanningId and highestPlanningSequenceOnOtherRefs cover milestones and decisions. The git common dir is already resolved (src/adapters/workspaces/local-workspaces.ts runs git rev-parse --git-common-dir and keeps commonDirectory), but nothing lists worktrees today. Ruled by opum-doc DEC-179; implement its outcome text exactly. This is part 1 of 4, order (1) then (4) then (2) then (3).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A create, for any id family (task, draft, milestone, decision), allocates its id under an exclusive lock held at <git-common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock.

The candidate id is one above the highest of: every local ref and remote-tracking ref (the current rule); the .quest working tree of every worktree, enumerated by git worktree list --porcelain, including uncommitted records; and the reservation ledger at <common-dir>/quest/reserved-ids.
The allocated id is appended to the reservation ledger before the lock is released.
A ledger entry is pruned once a record carrying that id is visible in any ref or worktree, or once it is older than 7 days.
Allocation performs no network access and no fetch; a stale lock older than 30s whose holder pid is gone is broken, and the run states that it did so.
A .quest directory with no Git repository behind it allocates exactly as today (working-tree-only, unchanged).

Proved both ways: two concurrent creates in two worktrees of one repository get distinct ids; with the lock and ledger disabled the same two concurrent creates collide (the mutation arm); and a create in a non-git directory is unchanged.

The allocator orders ids by their NUMERIC sequence, never by their characters, and a test proves it: ids crossing a digit boundary (9 -> 10 and 99 -> 100) allocate correctly, and the test fails when the comparison is changed to a string sort.

plan: 1. Confirm the numeric-comparator claim in the filing note against src/cli/main.ts, and confirm compareTaskIds is on dev (a28c8182).
2. Add GitPort.listWorktrees (git worktree list --porcelain) and its local-git adapter implementation.
3. New allocation module: common-dir alloc.lock, reservation ledger, per-worktree .quest scan, highest-id selection through compareTaskIds.
4. Rewire nextTaskId, nextDraftId and nextPlanningId through it; keep the non-Git path working-tree-only and unchanged.
5. Tests: two-worktree concurrency green, mutation arm with lock and ledger disabled red, non-git unchanged, 9 to 10 and 99 to 100 digit boundary, stale-lock break reported.
6. Measure the diff against the 400-line ceiling; if it does not fit, stop and report a split before opening the PR.
implementationNotes: Part (1) finding recorded by the filing session: the allocator ALREADY compares the numeric sequence, not string order -- src/cli/main.ts:1339-1342 (highestSequenceOnOtherRefs: Number() then Math.max), :1361-1365 (nextTaskId working-tree scan), :1413-1415 (nextDraftId), :1673-1675 (highestPlanningSequenceOnOtherRefs), :1700-1701 (nextPlanningId). Do not regress this; the added criterion is the missing digit-boundary test, not a comparator change. Existing allocation tests (test/qcli279-refs-aware-task-id-allocation.test.ts, test/qcli290-refs-aware-draft-planning-id-allocation.test.ts) exercise sequences that do not cross 9->10 or 99->100 for the task family.

DEC-181 / team-lead order change: HOLD this task until opum-ai/quest-cli#604 merges (tracked by QCLI-497). Part (1) then builds its numeric comparison ON the compareTaskIds introduced by #604 -- there is no second comparator. The digit-boundary criterion (index 7: 9 -> 10 and 99 -> 100, red under a string sort) still stands.

Dependency on QCLI-497 removed 2026-10-13 (team-lead instruction). QCLI-495 depended on QCLI-497 only to build its numeric id compare on #604 compareTaskIds rather than a second comparator. #604 is squash-merged on dev as a28c8182, so compareTaskIds (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts) is available; #605 and #606 still pending under QCLI-497 do not change it and are not prerequisites for part (1).

STOPPED BEFORE THE PR: the change does not fit the ~400-line ceiling, and it retires the input one existing test constructs. Branch feat/QCLI-495-worktree-aware-id-allocation, nothing pushed.

MEASURED SIZE: 873 insertions / 105 deletions across 5 files = 978 changed lines. New src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts is 394 lines (251 code, 119 comment, 24 blank) and carries lock acquisition, the 30s/dead-pid stale break, the ledger read/append/prune, and the two per-worktree record scans. The four-family rewiring is 185/105 in src/cli/main.ts. The new test file is 268 lines.

STATE: all 8 acceptance criteria are implemented and verified; lint (its 8 warnings are all pre-existing, in other files), format:check, typecheck and layer:check are clean. New suite test/qcli495-worktree-aware-id-allocation.test.ts: 6 tests, 6 pass. Full suite 1176 pass / 1 fail. Both mutation arms reproduced: changing the allocator one comparison (sort(compareTaskIds)) to a bare sort() turns the 9->10 / 99->100 test red (exit 5); disabling the lock and ledger turns the two-worktree concurrency test red 3 runs of 3 (exit 5, task_already_exists) -- DEC-179 m1 reproduced against the fix.

THE REGRESSION IS THE INTENDED EFFECT: test/qcli425-conflict-cause-and-echo.test.ts "a writer race stays distinguishable" builds its input as 16 concurrent auto-allocating task create in ONE worktree and asserts that some of them FAIL with the concurrent-change wording and no sentRevision. QCLI-495 removes exactly that race. Pre-fix control (stash, same invocation) 3 runs of 3 GREEN; post-fix 4 runs of 4 RED. The contract that test asserts is still live but now reachable only through an explicit --id writer racing an auto-allocating one, which is not deterministically constructible. So the PR cannot go green without a decision on that test.

OPTION A (recommended): one PR at 978 changed lines, with the size stated in the PR body. DEC-179 part (1) is a single outcome paragraph naming all four families and every acceptance criterion is in this task, so splitting means rewriting this task acceptance criteria and a ratified decision scope -- team-lead and opum-doc authority, not mine. Mitigation: three commits (module+port, wiring, tests) so the reviewer reads the mechanism before the wiring. The 400 figure is the skill own "roughly ... past that the reviewer skims" heuristic, not a gate.

OPTION B: split along the mechanism/proof seam -- 495a the port + module + four-family wiring + non-git path (about 605 changed lines), 495b the proof suite (about 373). It separates a change from its proof, which the fleet rules forbid, and neither half is comfortably under 400. Splitting by family breadth instead (task+draft, then milestone+decision) barely helps: the module is shared, so the larger half stays about 700.

QCLI-425 TEST, needs its own answer either way: (i, recommended) rewrite that one test to assert the invariant the change creates -- the same 16 concurrent creates in one worktree now all succeed with distinct ids, which is QCLI-495 at higher concurrency -- keeping the concurrent-wording contract on the arms that still reach it; or (ii) retire it and file a follow-up to re-cover the wording. (i) and Option A are what I would do next absent an answer.

ROUND 1 REVIEW, opum-ai/quest-cli#646 at head c2a49428a705e5575ce818d54d2cb2548556f37b: REQUEST CHANGES. Unit quest-cli-review-646-c2a4942, model claude-opus-5-5 (72/72 turns, read from its transcript by team-lead), worktree .claude/worktrees/review-646-c2a4942. Verdict file 15633 bytes, sha256 a3680721c8e3854abb502b0bc143d21f29276e211953bab9ebb3c5b2f27fc334, recorded verbatim below. The task returns to In Progress; findings 1 and 2 falsify ACs 1 and 4.

VERDICT quest-cli#646 @ c2a49428: REQUEST CHANGES

Two blocking defects in the mechanism. Each one undoes the guarantee DEC-179 (1) exists to give, and no current test can see either. All paths below are relative to the repo root; "id-alloc" means src/application/tasks/id-allocation.ts.

FINDINGS

1. BLOCKING. id-alloc:215. A process that breaks a stale lock then allocates without holding any lock.
- Problem: `if (await breakStaleLock(lockPath, now)) return true;` returns from acquireLock right after the unlink. It never goes back to `open(lockPath,"wx")`, so after a break no lock file exists. allocateId (:364-393) then runs the whole critical section unlocked. The comment at :191-192 says "the caller retries either way", but the code only retries when the unlink is lost.
- Failure scenario:
  - A quest process crashes holding alloc.lock, and more than 30s pass.
  - Worktrees B and C create at the same moment. B breaks the lock and goes straight in. C's next `open(wx)` succeeds because the file is gone, so C goes in too.
  - Both read the same ledger and the same worktree trees, and both mint N+1. That is m1 exactly.
  - B's releaseLock (:227-231) sees C's pid and correctly leaves the file alone, so nothing records the overlap.
  - Two breakers produce the same result: the loser of the unlink loops, its `open(wx)` succeeds, and it runs alongside the winner.
- This falsifies AC0 ("allocates its id under an exclusive lock") on exactly the path AC4/5 exercises. The stale-lock test (test/qcli495…:274-290) runs a single process, so it cannot see this.
- Fix: on a successful break, set `broke = true` and `continue` the loop. Return `broke` only after `open(wx)` succeeds.
- Test: plant a stale lock, then launch two concurrent creates in two worktrees and assert distinct ids. Alternatively, use the `git` seam: have a fake listWorktrees read lockPath during the critical section and assert it holds this pid.
- Secondary, MINOR: breakStaleLock has a TOCTOU. Breakers A and B both read lock L0 as stale. A unlinks it and creates L1. B then unlinks by path and deletes L1. Fix options: rename to a unique name and verify the renamed content is the stale one, or re-read pid and stamp immediately before the unlink.

2. BLOCKING. id-alloc:386-389. Every allocation deletes every other family's reservations.
- Problem: `kept = reserved.filter(e => (sequenceOfId(e.id, marker) ?? 0) > highestVisible)`. For an entry from another family, sequenceOfId returns null, `?? 0` makes it 0, and `0 > highestVisible` is always false because highestVisible is never below 0. writeLedger (:389) then rewrites the shared file with only this family's entries. So a task create wipes outstanding D-/M-/DEC-/Q- reservations, and vice versa.
- Failure scenario:
  - Worktree A runs `draft create`, reserves D-5 and releases the lock. Its record is not on disk yet; the window runs through readAll, canonicalisation and a wait of up to LOCK_WAIT_MS on .write.lock.
  - Worktree B runs `task create`. The ledger becomes [QCLI-k].
  - Worktree C runs `draft create`. A's D-5 is invisible in every ref and worktree and is gone from the ledger, so C mints D-5.
  - Result: add/add collision. The ledger exists for exactly this window.
- This falsifies AC4 (pruned only when visible or after 7 days) and the per-family correctness you asked about. Every test creates one family at a time, so nothing catches it.
- Fix: prune only entries where `sequenceOfId(e.id, marker) !== null && seq <= highestVisible`. Entries from other families are subject to the TTL only.
- Test: seed a fresh `{"id":"D-7"}`, run a task create, assert D-7 is still in the ledger, then assert a draft create returns D-8.
- Related NOTE: a workspace task prefix of D, M, DEC or Q shares its marker with that family's ledger entries. Tagging each ledger entry with its family would remove the overlap.

3. MINOR, but it needs your ruling. test/qcli425-conflict-cause-and-echo.test.ts:201-230. The rewritten create arm no longer tells fixed code from broken code.
- Problem: inside one worktree, distinct winner ids were already guaranteed before QCLI-495. An id collision loses either at the existence check (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:538, task_already_exists) or at the store-wide revision check (local-task-repository.ts:669). So `new Set(ids).size === wins.length` plus `wins.length > 0` would pass with the lock and ledger deleted (reasoned, not run).
- The only signal that separated fixed from broken was the win count: 4-7 of 16 without the fix, 15-16 with it. The flake fix dropped that bound. The test title "win with distinct ids (QCLI-495…)" overclaims, and Q2(i)'s "assert the new invariant" is not met by this test.
- Fix, cheap and load-tolerant: also assert that every loser carries `input.actualRevision`.
  - A loser of the revision check carries it, via local-task-repository.ts:669-676 to conflictFieldsOf to src/cli/main.ts:4811-4819.
  - An id-collision loser goes through task_already_exists to main.ts:4821-4838, which carries no input.
  - That separates "a conflict, not a collision" (the writer's own claim) from the m1 defect without a count bound. Under the mutation it goes red only if at least one loser hits the existence check, which is likely but timing-dependent.
  - Otherwise, rename the test to what it actually pins.

4. MINOR. The worktree scan is never tested on its own.
- Problem: every cross-worktree test is also satisfied by the ledger. So listWorktrees returning [] would pass all 9 tests. Yet the scan is the only protection for an uncommitted record older than 7 days, or one created with `--id` (idForCreate at main.ts:1304-1311 writes no ledger entry).
- Fix: in worktree A run `task create --id T-5` and leave it uncommitted, then auto-create in worktree B and expect T-6.

5. MINOR. id-alloc:312-314 and src/adapters/git/local-git.ts:217. A failed worktree enumeration silently degrades to the pre-fix behaviour.
- Problem: any non-zero exit from `git worktree list`, or any throw, becomes [], and allocation carries on without the worktree source.
- With a non-null common dir, the list always contains at least the current worktree, so [] can only mean the read failed.
- Fix: refuse, or at least warn, when the list is empty, in line with the fleet rule that a check must fail rather than pass when it reads zero inputs.

6. MINOR. id-alloc:216-219 together with main.ts:4869. The lock timeout does not fit the CLI contract.
- Problem: the timeout throws a plain Error with no code. It falls through to `failure("validation")`, which is exit 6 (src/domain/command-contract.ts:8). Contention is retryable and belongs under conflict, exit 5. local-task-repository.ts:655-663 already maps its own .write.lock timeout to conflict.
- The text "has held … for more than 10s" states how long we waited, not how long the lock was held.
- There is no hint. A live-pid lock is never broken, which is correct per DEC-179. But if the holder is wedged, or its pid was recycled, every create in every worktree fails until someone removes the lock by hand, and nothing tells them how.
- Fix: return a conflict with a hint naming the lock path, the holder pid and the lock's age, and saying that removing it is safe if that pid is not a quest process.
- No test covers the live-holder or timeout path.

7. MINOR. id-alloc:386-388. The prune rule differs from the DEC-179 text.
- DEC-179 prunes an entry "once a record with that id is visible". The code prunes every same-family entry at or below the highest visible id, whether or not its own record is visible.
- This is safe only while the visible high-water mark never drops. It drops if the top record disappears (worktree removed, `git checkout -- .quest`, branch deleted) while a lower reservation is still being written. That window is narrow.
- The benefit is that a losing create's orphan entry is cleared early. The task said "implement its outcome text exactly", so this needs your ruling or an exact-id prune.

8. MINOR. Claim 1 is false as worded: migration mints ids outside the allocator.
- Locations: src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts:314-324 (dotted-subtask mints), :477-485 (`${taskIdPrefix}-${highest+index+1}`) and :611-623 (`M-${n}`). They read this worktree only, with no refs, no lock and no ledger.
- This was there before the PR and is not a regression. DEC-179 says "A create", so migration may be out of scope.
- But the final summary says "Every id family … now allocates under an exclusive lock". Either narrow that to the create commands (task create, draft create/promote, milestone/decision create, question ask), all of which do go through allocateId, or file a follow-up.

9. MINOR. src/application/agents/guides.ts:164-187 is stale.
- The shipped guide (`quest instructions`) still says ids are "refs-aware" and that allocation "only consults refs".
- It does not mention the worktree scan, the ledger, the lock, the stale-lock stderr warning or the timeout.
- No CHANGELOG.md file is in the changed-file list, so I could not check for an Unreleased entry.

10. NOTE. id-alloc:251-260. The ledger write is not atomic.
- writeFile truncates and then writes. A SIGKILL in the middle leaves a truncated ledger, and readLedger (:242) drops the corrupt lines, losing reservations.
- Fix: write a temp file and rename it, as local-task-repository.ts:680-682 already does.
- Also id-alloc:208-213: if `handle.writeFile` throws after `open(wx)` succeeds, an empty lock file is left behind. It blocks every create for 30s, until the mtime rule breaks it.

11. NOTE. test/qcli495…:263-266.
- AC6's "no stray ledger" check reads `<store>/reserved-ids`, a path the code never writes even when it is broken, so that half proves nothing.
- The non-git path itself is correct. Outside Git, taskStoreRoot throws not_git_worktree (src/adapters/workspaces/local-workspaces.ts:133), so QUEST_TASK_STORE is the only reachable no-Git store, and main.ts:1286 returns null there.
- Two side effects:
  - QUEST_TASK_STORE pointing inside a real repo also skips the lock.
  - The catch-all at main.ts:1291 silently drops to the unlocked path on any workspace error, not only not_git_worktree.

12. NOTE. main.ts:1323. withAllocationNotice replaces stderr rather than appending to it. A success that already wrote stderr would lose it. Harmless today as far as I read.

CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND
- The lock is created atomically: `open(...,"wx")` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL) at id-alloc:208, not check-then-write.
- The lock is released in a finally (:391-393) on every exit after acquisition, including a throw. A failed record write happens after the release and leaves a burned ledger entry, not a held lock.
- The stale rule, apart from finding 1: older than 30s AND pid gone (:189-190). An unparseable or empty lock falls back to its mtime and is broken on age alone, which is documented at :178-181. A live pid is never broken. The wait is bounded at 10s.
- The ledger is written before the release (:389 runs inside the try).
- Ordering: highestId uses `sort(compareTaskIds)` (:134). The digit-boundary test is not vacuous: a bare sort makes it pick T-9 and collide with T-10.
- Layering: id-allocation.ts imports only domain and ports, plus node:fs, which application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts already does. listWorktrees is on the port and implemented in the adapter, and main.ts does the wiring.
- Every create site goes through allocateId: main.ts:2906, :3183, :3229, :3339 and :4084. Every one is wrapped in withAllocationNotice, including task create at :4151.
- Worktree enumeration takes every `worktree ` line, so bare, locked, prunable and missing entries are all included. An unreadable directory gives [] for that entry only.
- No network: GIT_TRACE reaches allocation's git calls, because local-git.ts:50 spawns with `{...Bun.env}`. The trace regex would catch a `git fetch`, `ls-remote` or `remote-https` child. It would not catch network access that bypasses git, such as a Bun fetch() or a `gh` call. There is no positive control (a deliberate `git fetch` traced to the same file and matched).
- Claim 8: the every-family test (:154-185) is not vacuous. created() throws on any non-zero exit, so Promise.all rejects. With the module off, neither worktree sees the other's uncommitted record, so round 1 collides deterministically. The writer's "6 of 9 red" is consistent with a mutation of commonDirectory → null, which turns off the whole module, worktree scan included. That means no arm shows the lock alone, or the ledger alone, to be load-bearing. Findings 1 and 2 surviving all 9 tests is the evidence of that gap.

CLAIM 7: (a), plus finding 3.
- Where it happens: a fresh create's snapshot is taken at src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:524 (`repository.readAll()`). At write time, local-task-repository.ts:668-677 compares `current.revision !== request.expectedRevision` while holding the per-worktree `.quest/tasks/.write.lock`. The repository's acquireLock timeout (:655-663) returns the same conflict shape.
- What it protects: the revision is a hash over the whole store, not over this record. It keeps cross-record validation honest: alias uniqueness, duplicate-id detection and canonicalizeTaskLinks for dependencies and parents (tasks.ts:538-548) all ran against a universe that may have changed. Two creates of different ids in one worktree conflict whenever one lands between the other's snapshot and its write. That is a real optimistic-concurrency conflict, unrelated to id allocation.
- Why it is safe: the check runs before the temp write and rename (:678-682), the lock is released in a finally (:705-707), so a loser writes no record and leaves no partial file.
- Why not (b): DEC-179 makes the allocation lock cover allocation plus the ledger append ("appended to the ledger before the lock is released"). It does not cover the record write. Getting 16 of 16 in one worktree would need either a create-level retry on an auto-allocated id, or a lock spanning the write. Both are behaviour beyond DEC-179 and would need a ruling.
- The losing create's ledger entry: it is not held for 7 days. It is pruned at the next same-family allocation once any higher id is visible, through the high-water prune in finding 7. Until then it only raises the floor and can never block. The cost is a gap in the sequence, which DEC-179 allows.
- Your call: the weaker assertion is the honest one about counts. But as written the arm cannot detect the defect (finding 3). Accepting it means accepting a deviation from Q2(i) that proves nothing about QCLI-495. The actualRevision assertion in finding 3 would make it discriminating.

UNVERIFIED BY FILE READ
- Whether the two blocking defects reproduce at runtime. Both are reasoned from the code; I ran nothing.
- Both mutation arms (lock bypassed red 3 of 3; bare sort red), and what exactly the "lock bypassed" mutation changed. I inferred commonDirectory → null from the 6-of-9 count.
- That the QCLI-425 create arm goes green with the lock and ledger removed (reasoned).
- That the actualRevision fix in finding 3 goes red under the mutation.
- Whether the no-network regex matches real GIT_TRACE output for a fetch.
- The test and CI results, including the 36 loaded runs and the 1244-pass gate.
- What the dev merge (399ffb58) changed. docs/log.md has no QCLI-495 line, and every 2026-10-20 line in it is a dev commit, so its diff looks inherited from the merge. I could not diff it to confirm.
- Whether a CHANGELOG entry exists.
- Whether layer:check passes; I only read the imports.
- Whether `git worktree list --porcelain` quotes paths containing newlines.

ROUND 1 FIXES, 2026-10-20. Both blocking defects were reproduced as failing tests BEFORE any fix (test/qcli495-id-allocation-unit.test.ts: lock absent during the critical section after a stale break; a draft reservation wiped by a task allocation), then fixed. 1 stale break now loops back to the exclusive create and reports the break only once the lock is held; breaking is a rename to a unique name plus a re-read, restoring with link (never over a newer lock) if the renamed lock was not the stale one; a failed lock-body write removes the lock. 2 the ledger entry carries its family (task, draft, milestone, decision, question), the prune is exact (drop only when THAT id is visible in a ref or worktree, or after 7 days), and another family entry is left to the 7-day limb. 3 (ruling) a lost revision check after allocation is a genuine conflict (the lock covers allocation plus the ledger append, not the record write): the 16-of-16 count is withdrawn; the QCLI-425 create arm asserts every loser carries input.actualRevision. 1. BLOCKING. id-alloc:239-253. The stale break can still remove a live holder's lock, so two allocators run the critical section together. This falsifies AC0's exclusivity on the stale-lock path, and AC0 is checked in .quest/completed/QCLI-495.json.
- Failure scenario (stale lock S planted, three creates):
  - (a) P1 and P2 both fail open(wx). Both read S at :234 and judge it stale.
  - (b) P1 renames S to parked1. :246 finds it is the same lock, P1 unlinks parked1 and loops, and open(wx) at :275 creates L1. P1 is now in the critical section.
  - (c) P2 reaches the rename at :239. It moves whatever is at lockPath, which is now P1's fresh L1. :246 finds it is not the stale lock, so P2 goes to link at :251.
  - (d) In the gap between P2's rename and link, lockPath does not exist. P3, waking from its 25ms poll or just starting, succeeds at open(wx) and holds L3.
  - (e) P2's link fails EEXIST and the error is swallowed at :251. :253 then unlinks parked2, the only copy of L1.
  - (f) P1 and P3 both run worktreeIds plus readLedger against the same state and mint the same id. Across two worktrees that is m1 exactly.
  - P1's releaseLock (:309-313) then sees P3's pid and leaves the lock alone, so nothing records the overlap.
- Two-party variant: on a filesystem where link() is unsupported (EPERM/ENOTSUP), :251 swallows the error and :253 unlinks L1 the same way. P2's next open(wx) then succeeds alongside P1, with no third process needed.
- The comment at :227-228 ("so it can never replace a newer holder's lock") is true but names the wrong property. The code cannot REPLACE a newer lock, but it can REMOVE one. That is the round-1 secondary, narrowed, not closed.
- The tests cannot see this:
  - The unit two-allocator test (:129-156) runs three allocators, but in-process. P2 and P3's renames are issued at about the same moment as P1's, so they almost always get ENOENT before P1 re-creates the lock.
  - The CLI test (:416-434) has only two processes per round.
  - Neither result is evidence the race is closed. The writer's own note records two-allocators as red only 2 of 3 even against the far wider c2a49428 window.
- Fix: never rename or unlink a lock you have not verified under exclusion.
  - Serialise the breakers through a second exclusive file, for example alloc.lock.break taken with open(wx), with its own short age-only stale rule.
  - Under that file, re-read alloc.lock and unlink it only if its pid and stamp still equal the stale reading.
  - While S exists, no one can open(wx) over it. With breakers serialised, nobody else can remove it, so the re-read then unlink has no TOCTOU, and the rename/link dance can go.
- Test: make the interleaving deterministic. Add an fs seam, or export breakStaleLock with a hook between the stale judgement and the removal, so a second breaker is forced to act after the first has re-acquired. Assert the first holder's lock file still exists and still carries its pid.

  - P1 finishes its critical section during P2's rename-to-link gap. releaseLock reads null at :310 and skips the unlink.
  - P2's link then restores L1, freshly stamped, with P1's pid, which is gone once P1 exits.
- Result: for about 30s every create in every worktree waits LOCK_WAIT 10s and fails with exit 5.
- The serialised-breaker fix in NEW 1 removes this too.

3. MINOR. main.ts:1287-1296. The workspaceCommonDirectory catch-all silently runs the create with no lock, no ledger and no worktree scan.
- This contradicts the fail-closed principle ruling 5 applied to the worktree list. Round 1 raised it inside finding 11, and it is unchanged.
- Failure scenario:
  - resolvedRoot() and resolvedCommonDirectory() each call resolveInitializedWorkspace separately (main.ts:1274 and :1291).
  - If the second call's git subprocess fails transiently, for example under 16 concurrent creates, commonDirectory is null.
  - allocateId then takes the no-Git path at id-alloc:451-456, with no warning, inside a real repository. That is the pre-fix allocator again.
- Fix: resolve the workspace once and take both worktreePath and commonDirectory from it. Or return null only for the QUEST_TASK_STORE case and rethrow everything else, since taskStoreRoot has already proved that a workspace resolves.

4. NOTE. id-alloc:238-253. A breaker killed between the rename at :239 and the unlink at :253 leaves alloc.lock.stale-<uuid> in <common-dir>/quest/ permanently, because nothing sweeps that pattern. If it was killed on the !sameLock branch before the link, the live holder's lock is gone as well (NEW 1 by crash). The NEW 1 fix removes the parked file entirely.

5. NOTE. id-alloc:335 and :480. Untagged ledger lines (family null) are under-reported.
- They are kept for 7 days but never consulted, which is the unsafe direction for a reservation.
- It is reachable only from unreleased c2a49428-era builds that were mid-create during an upgrade.

6. NOTE. id-alloc:65 against :54. LOCK_WAIT (10s) is shorter than STALE (30s).
- After a crashed holder, every create fails with exit 5 for up to 30s before any run can break the lock.
- The hint's "removing … is safe when pid N is not a quest process" covers it, because a dead pid qualifies, but CHANGELOG.md:24-27 presents the timeout only as the live-holder case.

finalSummary:
The create commands (task create, draft create and draft promote, milestone create, decision create, question ask) allocate ids under an exclusive lock at <git-common-dir>/quest/alloc.lock. The candidate is one above the highest id across every ref, every worktree .quest (git worktree list --porcelain, uncommitted included) and the reservation ledger <common-dir>/quest/reserved-ids; the id is appended to the ledger before the lock is released; a ledger entry is dropped when a record with that id is visible in a ref or worktree, or after 7 days; no fetch or network is used; a stale lock (over 30s, holder pid gone) is broken after which the breaker takes the lock itself, and the run says so; a live holder times out as a conflict (exit 5); an empty worktree list refuses the create as drift (exit 6); a .quest with no Git repository allocates as before; ordering is numeric through compareTaskIds. NOT covered: an explicit --id, creates on two machines (DEC-179 part 4), and the Backlog.md migration, which mints ids outside the allocator (QCLI-520). Verified by test/qcli495-worktree-aware-id-allocation.test.ts and test/qcli495-id-allocation-unit.test.ts; round 1 of the review (REQUEST CHANGES at c2a49428) found two blocking defects in the first version, both reproduced as failing tests and fixed, and its minors are recorded on this task.
